critical_code_review_comments: shops.py::accept_buy_offer treasury→owner-gold fallback is correct: it debits shops.treasury when treasury>=amount, otherwise debits users.currency; a single shop_buyback transaction is written with negative amount against the owner in both paths — this means gold spent from the treasury is ALSO recorded as an owner debit transaction. That is arguably fine for the payouts ledger but blurs the distinction between owner-purse spend and treasury spend; consider tagging the txn with a `paid_from` field or splitting into `shop_treasury_spend` vs `shop_buyback` so /ledger totals could later differentiate.

shops.py::accept_buy_offer re-lists the acquired item at `max(amount+1, round(amount*1.25))` — the +1 floor guarantees the resale is strictly greater than what the shop paid, which prevents an infinite-loop arbitrage on 1-2g items. Good defensive math.

shops.py::create_buy_offer stores a *snapshot* of the item at proposal time (name/description/stat_bonuses) — if the seller mutates their inventory item name via some other flow, the offer still shows the original. This is the correct choice for haggling integrity but worth documenting.

economy.py::leader_add_custom_offering slugifies via re.sub then dedupes with a while-loop appending -2/-3/... . Fine for low-volume manual entry, but if two leaders coin the same name simultaneously there is a TOCTOU window between find_one and insert_one. Consider a unique index on goods.slug for durability. Not a blocker.

Task-brief testIDs 'add-offering-btn' + 'treasury-deposit-input'/'treasury-withdraw-input' do NOT match the actual code. Actual web testIDs are `specialties-add-btn` and a single shared `treasury-amount-input`. All *functional* testIDs are present, but any downstream test suite copied verbatim from the brief will fail — main agent should reconcile the spec with the code (either rename in code or update docs).
